comment: Outlets whose public RSS/Atom feeds fill the weird-news front page (/api/weird, lib/weird.js). As with the brief (data/news-sources.json) we show only the outlet's own headline, its name, the time, a link to the story and the outlet's own link-preview image: never its description, opening paragraph or article text. Every item passes the moderation rules in lib/moderation.js first. Feed addresses come from the scout's research (the build sandbox could not reach any of them); the lead checked them on a Vercel preview with /api/weird?debug=1 on 16 Nov 2026 (results in each entry's 'checked' note). The owner should review and approve this list before launch. Guardian and NPR are left out on purpose: their feed terms are personal, non-commercial use only. Mix rule (owner request, 17 Nov 2026: 'not only UPI'): within each freshness band (under 2 days, 2-7, 7-14, older) the outlets take turns, each outlet's strangest story first, and no outlet may take more than 3 of the first 12 feed stories or 10 of the first 30 while other outlets have stories (LIMITS.mix in lib/weird.js); editor's picks stay on top and are not counted. On 17 Nov 2026 the build sandbox could reach theconversation.com, www.atlasobscura.com, www.smithsonianmag.com, www.mentalfloss.com and www.livescience.com; every other host was refused by the sandbox's network proxy, so those feeds and terms are unverified here.
fields: name: shown as the outlet. section: the outlet's section the feed covers. home: the outlet's page we link to (also its own-site boundary for og:image reads). enabled: false = the feed is still read for ?debug=1 but none of its stories is used. stale: the date its feed was last seen with nothing from the past 14 days (kept: it may post again). images: false = no picture is read or shown (not even one the editor supplies for a pick), and its article pages are never fetched. imageHosts: the outlet's own image CDN hosts (exact names; a subdomain of one also counts), for pictures the editor gives a pick in the reviewer console: a pick's picture must be on the story's own site (the same registrable domain) or on one of these. review: true = a higher-risk outlet; its items appear only if moderation passes, never above a regular outlet's item, at most 3 at a time. minWeirdness: the lowest weirdness() score (lib/weird.js) a story needs to run; 0 for an odd-news desk, 1 for an outlet's own offbeat section, 2 for a general feed. cap: at most this many of its stories at once (default 8, 3 for review outlets); entries with the same name share one count, so give them the same cap. maxAgeDays: how far back a story may be (default 14, at most 90); evergreen outlets get longer windows, and a story older than 14 days always sorts after every fresher one (lib/weird.js freshness bands). listicles: false = drop listicles, quizzes and evergreen explainers. categoryHints: lower-case words found in the feed's own <category> labels -> our category. filter: when present, an item is kept only if one of its feed categories contains one of 'categories' or its URL path contains one of 'paths'. exclude: an item is dropped when its headline contains one of 'titles' (whole words, any case) or its URL path one of 'paths'. licence: what we know about the terms. terms: what the outlet's robots.txt and terms say about reading its feed and article pages and showing its preview images, and how we checked. comment: why this entry's settings are what they are. evaluated (top level): candidates looked at and not added, with the reason; they are never read.
